reviews.title: Paying for sync
reviews.text:
I purchased my first Withings product on October 16, and I was genuinely excited and happy with my purchase. I had a very positive first impression of the brand and was looking forward to becoming a long-term customer.

However, after discovering that importing and syncing my health data with Apple Health requires a paid subscription, my entire perception of the product has changed.

Honestly, I am extremely disappointed. I find it hard to believe that a $15 smart scale I owned previously could automatically sync my data with Apple Health at no additional cost, while a much more expensive Withings product requires me to pay a recurring subscription for what I consider a basic functionality.

I purchased your scale expecting a premium product and a seamless experience, not to discover that essential data integration comes with an additional recurring fee.

This policy has genuinely made me regret my purchase. What initially made me excited about Withings has now become a source of frustration, and I cannot understand why a company that positions itself as a premium health technology brand would restrict such a fundamental feature behind a subscription.

reviews.title: Bait and switch
reviews.text:
I bought this scale with the explicit understanding that it would sync seamlessly with Apple Health. While it functioned adequately for a period, the company has now unilaterally stripped away the ability to export data to Apple Health—or any other third-party platform—and locked these basic capabilities behind a $10 monthly paywall.
Extorting customers to pay a recurring fee just to retain the fundamental features they already paid for is completely unacceptable.
If a company wishes to launch new products under a subscription model, that is their prerogative. However, pushing a firmware update years down the line to intentionally downgrade a product and strip away its core functionality is predatory, deceitful, and disgraceful business practice.

reviews.title: Too Many Forced Distractions
reviews.text:
Thank you for fixing the lockup with the “walking“ feature, which trapped users in an inescapable software backwater. Much appreciated. I have one other request: Can you please give us a choice to opt out of the app’s many functions that we don’t want?

Case in point: Please make it possible to remove references to MyFitnessPal, software that I used long ago, but not anymore, because it has been surpassed by its far more sophisticated rival, Cronometer. 

It would also be helpful if we could opt out of your questionably useful “Today’s Missions”, which are poorly executed and profoundly outdated, often focusing on studies that have been paid for by companies that can benefit from them. 

Some people might like these extras, but I find them completely useless and distracting. I value ability to control the powerful features of your hardware, but not at the expense of having to be distracted and annoyed by unnecessary fluff. 

Simply let users choose whether we’d like to use these extras or not. This is especially relevant because now, unlike before, you are forcing us to wade through lots of distractions just so we can utilize the sophisticated features of your hardware, for which we already paid a premium price.

reviews.title: Great Hardware Ruined by a Greedy, Buggy App and Paywalled Basics
reviews.text:
I wish I could give zero stars. The physical scale/watch is fine, but the iOS app is an absolute disaster that makes the entire ecosystem worthless. Withings has completely lost touch with its user base, prioritizing subscription revenue over basic functionality.
 
The Paywall is Anti-Consumer: It is infuriating to spend hundreds on a device, only to have core health metrics locked behind the "Withings+" subscription. Users on the r/withings forum have repeatedly pointed out that features like Vascular Age and Electrodermal Activity (EDA) are suddenly restricted unless you pay up, even though these were previously accessible or promised as part of the hardware purchase . It feels like a bait-and-switch.‌￼
 
FDA Approval Means Nothing Here: You mentioned the FDA approval—it's a joke in this context. Even though Withings touts its FDA-cleared ECG, the app experience is so broken that the data is useless. Furthermore, users have discovered that even with FDA clearance, Withings still puts up arbitrary barriers (like requiring a "prescription" for ECG in the US) while simultaneously failing to deliver on basic data syncing . The hardware might be medically approved, but the software is not fit for purpose.‌￼‌￼

reviews.title: Worked for years, then Withings stopped supporting it
reviews.text:
My Withings Body scale worked well for years. Then one day, with no action on my part, it stopped recognizing users and stopped remembering prior weigh-ins. I reset it to fix that and it has not paired with my iPhone since. It gets stuck on the first setup step, every time. The cause is a known firmware incompatibility with current iPhones that Withings' own community forum has documented since October 2025 (search "Unable to pair and setup Body+ with iPhone 17 Pro"). The hardware is fine. Withings stopped keeping its firmware current, and the scale became a paperweight.

Customer support took almost two weeks of back and forth. Their first reply came in Catalan. They had me run troubleshooting steps I had already done, then concluded the scale needed replacing. Because it is outside the two-year warranty, the offer was 30% off a new scale, which now costs more than double what I paid. That is about $100 to replace a working product that Withings itself broke, with no reason to expect the next one would last any longer. Three rounds of asking for a supervisor or any better resolution got the same scripted answer.

A bathroom scale should not have an expiration date set by a phone update. If you want a scale that will still work in five years, buy one that doesn't depend on Withings keeping up.

reviews.title: Where is the data
reviews.text:
I just bought their latest scale model in body fit.


1 star — Plenty of distractions, no clear access to my data

I bought this Withings scale for the extensive body measurements advertised on the website. My main expectation was simple: step on the scale, open the app, and clearly see my measurements.

Instead, the app is cluttered with advertisements, unrelated content, and an intrusive AI assistant asking questions I have no interest in answering. Meanwhile, I cannot find a clear overview of the biomarkers that convinced me to buy the scale.

I can see some weight and body composition information, but even viewing basic measurements such as weight and body fat percentage feels unnecessarily difficult. If the other advertised measurements are available, I have not been able to find them.

The core problem is access to my own data. An expensive scale promising detailed measurements should make those measurements easy to view and track. In my experience, the app fails at that basic job.

The new change means if you have a new account, your scale, for example, will no longer sync your weight and body composition data for free, which it used to be able to do. If you have an account created prior to October 13th, 2026, it’s only a matter of time before Withings paywalls the feature to the paid Withings+ subscription. reviews.title: Awful app
reviews.text:
They want you to use all of their profits and the app as your primary health screen.  This means there are a bunch of options that are front and center in the app that are 100% useless to someone that only uses the scale. 
The scale metrics are designed in interesting ways, but every metric seems to require 3 or more clicks to get to.  For example, the segmental analysis has to be viewed by clicking into a map of a body and then clicking into each body segment. When you do click into these things, you see percentages, but not the actual weight of each segment. Sometimes the metrics aren’t there at all — LBM needs to be viewed by leaving the app and opening Apple health.  So withings has the info; it just doesn’t show you the info.
Advice to withings: give users a data-centric view with all data in a single view that doesn’t require multiple screens.  Don’t mess up the UI by trying to get me buy into more of the Withings’ ecosystem.  In short — prioritize the user; not what you want the user to do.

Why make profile update mandatory, especially when the data is very unlikely to change…my name, height, DOB! Rubbish design.

reviews.text: Was working fine until update, since then I’ve had to disassociate and reconnect my scale but now it doesn’t sync with apple health

reviews.title: Horrible to use
reviews.text: Difficult

reviews.title: I can no longer see past date
reviews.text: After the latest update it is no longer possible to view past readings for muscle mass and fat mass. In the list it just shows the relative change since the previous reading which is completely useless due to daily variation. I can no longer tell what my readings were for a day last year.

reviews.title: Fed up
reviews.text: Have to log out and in each day to get the app to refresh.

reviews.title: Sync to Apple Health doesn’t work
reviews.text: Used to work, now not. For at least a year.

reviews.title: Latest app release version is terrible
reviews.text:
The latest app version is terrible. When looking at data from smart scales, if you select any other timeframe for weight, suddenly %fat and % muscle appear and it squashes the graph for weight. Therefore can’t easily see or track progress of average weight or %fat or %weight. MUCH prefer the previous app layout as it was so much easier to read graphically than this version. Not sure why Withings wanted to change it as it was great before! 

Please revert!!

reviews.title: Pointless Update
reviews.text: The only way to look at your weight history now is under ‘body composition’ which squashes the weight information up so tightly to fit the fat and muscle graphs on that it’s barely usable. Why can’t they leave things alone?

reviews.title: Weighing scales
reviews.text: Since I got these scales their on and off as I don’t get reading so have to do it lots of times their not worth the money  it just don’t send to my app even when I’ve down downloads refreshed and changed battery

reviews.title: Going downhill with Ai bloat
reviews.text: The app is getting worse, version 26.40 now adds an immovable Ask health questions AI prompt at the bottom. It reduces the  amount of useful info you can see on the screen before scrolling. Combined with the lost screen space of the Readiness / Health score etc icons at the top of the app it’s become harder to see useful info at a glance.

reviews.title: Awful
reviews.text: Unable to add family members. Phones log into wrong profiles. Unable to switch. Corrupted data.

reviews.title: % weight?!
reviews.text: This was a great app. The latest update brought a lot of good ideas, and one utterly dumb concept. Instead of showing how many kilos you lost, it tells you what % of your weight you lost. This is a ridiculously stupid way to display this data.

reviews.title: Good

reviews.text: Losing the time setting while charging, requiring manual intervention.O2 check function stop working and even a reset does not fix it. Was good but now is bad

Far too crummy.

reviews.title: New version ruined it
reviews.text: Please bring back weight only. We don’t always want to see muscle and fat.

reviews.title: Very Disappointed
reviews.text: My witching’s watch continually disconnects from the app.  I have to reinstall the most times to get it to connect.  It also loses Tim quite quickly once disconnected.  I find most metrics it measures inaccurately.  Pulse it will only measure when at rest, if I’m moving, even walking at relaxed pace it either reports an error or just reverts to previous pulse.  Sleep measurements are woefully inaccurate also.  Oxygen sats however do work pretty well but all other features are unreliable.  On the plus side it is a very good quality build on the watch.  I’ve lost count of the number of times I’ve caught it on walls or metalwork but there’s no visible damage to the watch.

reviews.title: Average
reviews.text: Difficult to navigate record exercise very well from your Apple Watch

reviews.title: Useless
reviews.text: Takes data from two different devices at two different addresses but presents the data as from a single source, despite the obvious fact the two devices measure differently. How do I view the data from only one of the devices?

reviews.title: It was great before the paywalls started
reviews.text: The company expects the customer to buy an very expensive device that some functionality (for now, be sure paywalls will increase) are behind subscription fees and now comes the BEST: they launched a program where users will volunteer the data they cannot get through their devices by answering surveys about their daily routine, health conditions and treatments. Do the math: smart scale £349, blood pressure monitor £229, thermometer £229, subscription £99/year and then they want you to volunteer to help them improve their algorithms so they can rise up the subscription prices and charge you more to use a product you already bought and helped them build which without your data they would have to pay people to be able to get. Whoever signs up for this programme should at least get all functionalities for their devices free for life. If not get dividends from the algorithm they built

reviews.title: Data is messed up and not reliable
reviews.text: Random days in the past have 0 steps while Apple Health has steps. Re-installing the app makes the steps come back but disappear on other days. Lots of syncing issues with other data from Apple Health, especially sleep data. Customer support is useless - doesn't know anything other than to ask to reinstall the app. I've been using the app for the last 15 years due to their scale, and in recent years since they started doing paid subscriptions, it really went down and unreliable - syncing issues, broken menus, etc. Unhappy and looking for alternative scale that can sync with Apple Health.

reviews.title: The App is totally user unfriendly
reviews.text: Since the latest updates, I can no longer access my past activities. While manually adding activities via the “+” button is straightforward, there appears to be no way to locate those activities afterwards.The overall user experience is frustrating, as finding a solution to any issue seems to require searching through the Community forums.

reviews.title: Sub Optimal
reviews.text:
For a premium piece of hardware to have such subpar software, it takes some nerve to then incessantly push an annual subscription model. I'd had my new scales for less than a day before numerous problems became apparent. 

The app is unable to find my 2G network (and incompatible with 5G), while every other app can. It constantly needs manual Bluetooth reconnection. It doesn't sync properly with Apple Health, despite accessing the relevant permissions. So, in summary, the app functions by occasionally providing inaccurate data I can only access by manual connection. 

The app, replete with the usual nauseating infantile infographics, seems more concerned with pushing the same irritating health tips that anyone with an ounce of common sense knows. Stop this. Just give me the data in a clear, accurate and reliable manner. I can do the rest. Obviously, I won't be subscribing.

reviews.title: Some good parts
reviews.text:
The weight graphs and body composition are really interesting but after the latest update some of the graphs for BMI etc have disappeared and just show a score. 
The biggest problem I have with this app is the step syncing. I have it linked to Apple Health to sync steps from my Garmin. I’ve also tried linking to MyFitnessPal for the steps, making sure to only have 1 app sending step info to Withings. Every time I open the Withings app, it updates the steps, it doesn’t check if steps have already gone in and therefore inflates the number of steps. So it is never accurate and really frustrating. I’ve tried everything, uninstalling, removing all data, different configurations or which app reads and writes data, nothing stops it. I’ve even turned off background refresh and live updates and tested every combination thoroughly, it still over inflates the steps, as if it receives the data multiple times and never checks if the data is already there. Very annoying, so I’ll be switching brands of scales unfortunately.

reviews.title: Used to be great
reviews.text:
Way back when it really was Withings, the scale was a bit finicky but once connected it worked and worked for years. 
Then when Nokia took over it went down hill. The interface got changed. Everything became  clunky to operate. It only mattered at battery change time.  But again once it was finally working it worked. 
     Apparently the co-founder and former chairman bought it back in 2018 but the interface remained. The prices went up and the features got removed. 
     We have the original Smart Body Analyzer with mass and fat and cardio. Now that same model is way way more than we paid. But our scale is still working great!  It’s the software that’s horrible. They keep adding features that I’m not sure who really uses, making it difficult to find my weight and trend—the original reason for getting it. Multiperson tracking gets crossed up, it forgets which person you are, makes unassigned measurements, or ignores one of the trackees. 
     If you can deal with all that and get it straightened out, it may be OK. If you’re a solo person working with just one trackee, it may be OK. I wish someone in software development would look back at the original design and bring those features and implementation back to the forefront.

reviews.title: Harmful Messaging
reviews.text: I am extremely concerned about the negative messaging from the Withings App and its potentially harmful effects, looking at body dysmorphia and general mental health.  As someone who has run almost daily my entire adult life, as a 52 year old, I found the knee arthroscopy I had last summer really hard to deal with.  So, I shifted my focus to lifting heavy in the gym, bulking for around 6 - 9 months, changing my eating habits and taking creatine monohydrate to maximise my gains.  I have now started 12 weeks of hybrid training, with a caloric deficit to get the “shredded” look I want, mixing PPL gym sessions and running / cardio to maintain muscle and to lose fat.  The Withings App is full of the wrong kind of messages, telling me I’m “overweight”, based on a BMI that has no context.  I am carrying at least 1 - 2Kg more muscle than I was a year ago and probably a similar amount of water.  The app, as with many others seems to be built on the premise that I am looking to lose weight and that I have struggled to do this in the past.  Neither of these is appropriate.

reviews.title: Big Brother Hiding In Your Scale
reviews.text: They want waaay to much data, and waaay to much permission to share that data. Last time I updated the app, it locked me out unless I told them they could share my data with whomever they wanted. I didn’t update my permissions, and quit using the app. A few months later, I opened it and it no longer asked for that permission, just a screen asking me to update my personal details, which either means they got some push back from customers, or they’re doing it anyway without my permission. I’ve got a crazy idea - how bout you create a business model that makes a profit by selling me a product - what a radical idea - rather than trying to profit off my data. Or, here’s an even crazier idea. How about you offer me an app that is solely there to enhance your product and my experience, rather than your bottom line - one that puts the customer first. Don’t get me wrong, the scale works great, and the app is convenient. But, if I were to do it again, I’d just buy a mechanical scale and a pad and pencil. You know, the kind of tools that you pay hard earned money for, and then you use them, rather than the reverse. Call me crazy, but I have no interest in being used by my scale.

reviews.title: Hardware fantastic, software garbage
reviews.text:
The scales themselves are excellent, but this app is an absolute nightmare. They've seemingly sacrificed usability and functionality to push subscription options everywhere.

Our scales were recording my weight and body comp fine, but my girlfriend was onto getting weight, why? Who knows and there's no way to figure it out via the app, those useful options (like seeing users or profiles attached to your scales) just don't exist. Once you've shared it, there's no list of those you've shared it with. Just a "delete everyone else" button. There's no way to manually create a profile to test this. And for some reason you can't enable eyes closed mode and athlete mode.

There's just masses of functionality missing. But at least it syncs to apple health so I rarely, if ever, have to use the app

reviews.title: Used to be great, but...
reviews.text:
Back when the first Scanwatch was introduced, the app was fantastic. Everything just worked as expected, and it was highly customizable, only surfacing the data that I asked for. Eventually, however, more and more functionality was removed from the app, the Withings+ subscription was pushed, and a number of bugs surfaced. 

I just bought a Scanwatch 2 to replace my busted Scanwatch, because in spite of the app, I do really like the watch itself, and the new Healthsense 4 update really seems to have improved the quality of the readings. 

Unfortunately, the app is still a mess. There's no option to turn off the "daily missions," which are just pointless re-introductions to Scanwatch features I've known about for years now. The metrics I chose to Surface in the "My Focus" section just seem to change at will based on the day, and they're either always out of order or a metric that I previously selected (such as sleep oxygen) just disappears from the list entirely. Furthermore, there is no way to reorder the menu bar across the top. I want it to display the features I use the most often, not the ones like "Vitalite" that are locked behind the subscription. The lack of customization and reduced functionality is frustrating. I'm committed to sticking with it for as long as I have my Scanwatch 2, but I sure hope that the developers make some changes and that the app quality returns to what it once was.

reviews.title: Annoyingly bad app for expensive devices.
reviews.text: I bought two Withings devices before realising how bad the ‘ecosystem’ around them was. I got the BPM Core first. First sign of trouble was when I bought it to the doctor’s surgery to compare readings. It did not update the readings to the App so you have to catch them as they flash across the dot matrix on the device itself and write them down (with a quill pen?). This seems to be because it uses WiFi not Bluetooth for this so it has to be in range of my home WiFi. Foolishly then I bought a Body Cardio scale. This occasionally gets a heart rate reading, but mostly it fails. Worse the App has now stopped recording the perfectly reliable HR readings from the pressure cuff! Then the scales for no apparent reason switched to displaying weight in stones, pounds and ounces and I cannot find the setting for this anywhere in the App. Eventually resort to the Internet where kind folk inform me I cannot change this back to civilised kilograms in the App but have to crawl on the floor like a toddler and change it using a single-button hardware interface! Really Withings! Do Better!

reviews.title: One massive flaw.
reviews.text:
I spent years with my original Withings scanwatch. I loved the look, the feel, the way it worked. The app is decent too as far as I can tell. 

The flaw? 

Well, recently the back fell off my watch. Still attached by wires to the sensors, but wholly unattached. Fair enough it had outlasted the guarantee, and never missed a beat but that’s undermined entirely by the construction. 

In my mind, a watch shouldn’t be glued together. Maybe a kids watch, but not a “certified medical device”. 
Not a watch costing several hundred pounds. 
Not one so well supported. 

But the whole of the back of the watch is glued on by a 1mm wide flange. 
The whole of the back of every one of their watches is glued on. 

These are activity tracking monitors. Glue and sweat don’t generally mix well. 
Even Casio screw the backs on their watches. 

So after years as a fan, I’m out. I’d have worn that watch for years. Even without the app but I don’t have that opportunity. 
There’s nothing smart about a smartwatch that’s glued together. 

I’ve gone over to mechanical watches and proper, solid engineering. I recommend you start with a Seiko. 
No more apps, tracking, updates, charging, just an incredibly good watch. 

Complication is fine, if it’s backed by longevity. 
But these watches are disposable, once they back comes off there is no repair available. Even from Withings. 
You’re done. 

Enjoy!

reviews.title: 2 Great years then Drama
reviews.text:
It’s frustrating nowadays buying new products and they don’t last meanwhile my 79-year-old father has a deep freezer that his family had before he was born that has never had any maintenance or any problems and everything in that freezer stays frozen forever so besides that point, what I’m talking about is, I’ve had the scale for two years. It worked great then glitches started happening.

The first thing is and it still is a problem. I can no longer edit my weight goals. I used to be able to edit my goals. It won’t let me do it. I’ve deleted the app. Put the app back on nothing! 

Next, then the scales stopped working for over a month out of the blue. I did contact CUSTOMER SERVICE. And it took many tries before the final outcome was, I just have to get a new scale. Soooo while waiting for me to have the money for a new scale, The scale decided to start working a month and a half later, but I still cannot edit my weight goal on the App. Super frustrating. Don’t think I’ll buy this brand again
